title: Ten years of recuperation
summary: Illness ended his ambition; he recovered intermittently until 1951.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: If I had had any ambition before that, if I had any proclivity to be ambitious, that just knocked it out of me. It caused me to read a lot and I don't regret it, but it was a lot of years sitting around.
Well not consecutively, it went intermittently beginning January, '42 and I was still on the recuperating schedule all through '51; so let's say about ten years.

After that I said the hell with it. When we got Sauter-Finegan, I put a cot on the bus and made sure I got a lot of rest, but I think what saved me there was the laughter. There were a bunch of kooks on that band and it was never boring, I thought it would be awful. In those days we had inherited European chefs and the frozen
food scene had not become epidemic as it is today, so that we ate well. I thought it would be awful, but it wasn't. So I survived, but I think the laughter had the most to do with it.
Especially when you're on the road; that can make a big difference.
